title: Imaging-based registry for treatment quality, quality of life, and symptom control following cerebral neuromodulation procedures
summary:
The goal of this registry is to better understand potential risks and side effects in all patients who have undergone procedures to modulate brain activity in Freiburg since 2013. The study examines the circumstances under which complications—such as bleeding or reactions in the surrounding tissue—occur.

In addition, various medical data will be compared to identify new correlations. This includes, on the one hand, results from imaging procedures (such as brain scans) and from the planning of the procedures, and, on the other hand, the actual treatment success in patients.

Specifically, the study will examine:

Whether the precise structure and connectivity of the treated brain region influence how well the therapy works (for example, in terms of symptom improvement, quality of life, or side effects)

Whether this structure and connectivity are related to results from specialized examinations (e.g., PET scans)

Whether individually tailored planning of the procedure—based on brain connectivity—improves treatment success

Whether there is a correlation between brain connectivity and the test results collected during the procedure

In addition, the long-term disease progression of patients who have received deep brain stimulation (DBS) in Freiburg is systematically recorded and evaluated.

interventions.name: Clinical outcomes (especially bleeding complications) and long-term effects of DBS and other neuromodulation therapies will be assessed. For this purpose, parts of the routinely collected data of the control visits will be documented in the registry.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. All patients who undergo or have undergone since January 1, 2013, a cerebral neuromodulation procedure (DBS implantation or lesioning procedure) at the University Medical Center Freiburg in collaboration with the Department of Stereotactic and Functional Neurosurgery
2. Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
None
